decisions.note: p1 prototype had no way to open the saved link; client asked for click-to-open before maker built it.
Auto-fetched title/description had no edit path in p1; client demanded post-save editing.
Duplicate-save behavior was untested/unshown; client explicitly asked to see re-save-of-existing-url handling.
Edit pop-up (styles A/B/C) had no tagging field at all; client asked for labels to be added.
No personal note field existed, and later no markdown-style shape (bold/bullets); client requested both in turn.
Of 3 label-entry styles offered, only 'C - type with suggestions' actually implements tag autocomplete; client selected C specifically because it steers to existing tags.
Tags were purely decorative (no click-to-filter); client called this out as the missing payoff of labeling.
No free-text search existed after topic filtering shipped; client asked for a search box over title/description/note/url.
Multi-word search required exact adjacent order; client corrected this to 'all words anywhere, any order' with quotes for exact phrase.
Read-later/unread lens was never built despite being part of the original goal; client re-raised it until maker delivered it.
Read-later pile only supported marking one item at a time; client asked for bulk 'sweep several as read' when the pile grows.
Bulk select/act existed only inside the To-read pile; client asked for the same select-and-batch power (tags, read/unread) in the main library.
No permanent delete existed anywhere in the app until this point; client asked 'where's the throw-it-in-the-bin?'.
Archive/'set aside' concept was entirely absent; maker only offered delete-with-undo, and client redirected to request a reversible archive shelf.
No sort control existed; client flagged the missing ability to reorder (oldest-first, alphabetical) before agreeing to call the design done.
Import/export were never mentioned; client raised bringing an existing bookmark mountain in and getting links back out.
No snapshot/never-lose-a-link mechanism existed; client raised it after being shown a dead link with nothing preserved.
Import presentation never mentioned preserving original save dates; client demanded original dates carry over so 'oldest first' stays meaningful.

Maker offered a 'readable text extraction' as the default snapshot instead of the reference's literal local-HTML single-file capture; client picked 'readable is the must-have' without flagging the fidelity/format gap versus the spec.
PDF handling for snapshots was unaddressed; client asked whether PDFs keep the actual file rather than a scrape.
Independent public-archive backup was never surfaced; client suggested it as 'belt and braces' for precious links.
Saved search/bundle feature was never presented; client asked to pin repeated filter combinations as one-click shortcuts.
Topic exclusion (NOT) was missing from the topic bar (only AND/OR existed); client asked to be able to 'carve a topic out'.

Client asked for display comfort settings but then narrowed scope to only text-size and light/dark, leaving 'displayed items'/persisted default-sort settings from the reference unaddressed and unchallenged.
Real-world testing showed YouTube links got a flat/generic auto-fetched title; client flagged the concrete failure and it was fixed via a dedicated fetch path.
Editing a url into an existing bookmark's url was not yet guarded against creating a duplicate; client pre-emptively demanded the same dedupe guarantee apply to the edit path.
Tag suggestion/dedup didn't normalize case/whitespace ('Recipes ' vs 'recipes'); client asked for the anti-fork net to catch that too.

Maker proposed deferring snapshot backfill for pre-existing/imported links to a later enhancement; client rejected that deferral given imported links are the most fragile, forcing an on-demand 'keep a copy now' capability into the current layer.
